_comment: Trashlands: keep FTB Ultimine off the salvage economy.
The rule is narrower than 'everything worldgen places'. Two kinds of block are here:
1. Scrap piles - what a worldgen feature heaps up as a dig-for-scrap target.
2. Surface ground - coarse dirt, mound ground, stained ground. The surface is the board
reclamation and encroachment are played on, so stripping it in one hold is terraforming.
3. Overworld bulk stone - minecraft:deepslate, which garbage.json sets as the default_block
under two blocks of coarse dirt. Owner call 2026-09-07. The starting plain is where this
pack's scarcity is designed, and an infinite quarry two blocks under it undoes that.
Deliberately NOT here, and it is a load-bearing omission:
- recompile:techno_organic_waste, the Compacted Depths' bulk stone (its noise_settings
default_block). It drops itself, so it is a building material, not a scrap pile, and with
slag_rubble and ancient_sculk already excluded, adding it would leave NOTHING vein-mineable
in that dimension. Excluding deepslate does not do that to the overworld - trees, crops,
farmland and player builds all remain - which is why the two are treated differently.
The Depths is an earned region where fast quarrying is a reward; the plain is not.
Ultimine ships this tag empty, so replace:false appends rather than overwrites.
This governs BREAKING only. The right-click hoe/shovel paths read ftbultimine:farmland_tillable
and ftbultimine:shovel_flattenable, which ship containing coarse dirt and are NOT overridden.
Add any new Recompile scrap-pile block here when one lands.
